in response to the very high 3-factor correlations (EF-Reasoning r=.98, EF-Language

Depends on `wide_scores`, built in _08-sem.qmd's `prep-sem` chunk (same task columns:

```{r prep-bifactor}
#| dependson: sem-factors
```

```{r bifactor-model}
# Bifactor model: a general factor g loads on all nine indicators; three
# orthogonal group factors (reasoning, ef, language) capture variance specific
# to each domain over and above g. Each group factor keeps >= 3 indicators
# (a requirement for bifactor identification), matching the group factors
# used in the correlated 3-factor model (mdl_3f) in _08-sem.qmd.

mdl_bifactor <- "
  g         =~ mrot + matrix + math + mg + sds + hf + vocab + trog + tom
  reasoning =~ mrot + matrix + math
  ef        =~ mg + sds + hf
  language  =~ vocab + trog + tom

  # orthogonality: general factor uncorrelated with group factors,
  # and group factors uncorrelated with each other
  g ~~ 0*reasoning
  g ~~ 0*ef
  g ~~ 0*language
  reasoning ~~ 0*ef
  reasoning ~~ 0*language
  ef        ~~ 0*language

  g ~ age_c
"

fit_bifactor <- sem(
  mdl_bifactor, data = wide_scores,
  estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", std.lv = TRUE,
  optim.method = "nlminb",
  control = list(iter.max = 50000, rel.tol = 1e-6)
)
# summary(fit_bifactor, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
```

```{r bifactor-propriety-check}
# lavInspect(..., "converged") only tells you the optimizer stopped; it says
# nothing about whether the solution is admissible. Bifactor models routinely
# "converge" to Heywood cases (negative residual variances, |loading| > 1)
# when a group factor has little variance left over once g is partialled out
# -- exactly the failure mode you'd expect if the reviewers' "one general
# factor" concern is right. Check explicitly rather than trusting convergence.

bifactor_proper <- lavInspect(fit_bifactor, "post.check")

bifactor_neg_var <- parameterEstimates(fit_bifactor, standardized = TRUE) |>
  filter(op == "~~", lhs == rhs, std.all < 0) |>
  select(variable = lhs, est, std.all)

if (!bifactor_proper || nrow(bifactor_neg_var) > 0) {
  warning(
    "fit_bifactor is an improper solution (post.check = ", bifactor_proper,
    "). Negative residual variances: ",
    paste(bifactor_neg_var$variable, collapse = ", "),
    ". Fit-index comparisons below (CFI/RMSEA/AIC/BIC) are not trustworthy ",
    "for an inadmissible solution -- report the impropriety itself as the ",
    "finding, don't just cite the fit indices."
  )
}
```

```{r bifactor-fit-compare}
# Compare the bifactor model against the correlated 3-factor model (fit_3f,
# from _08-sem.qmd) on fit indices, and (where nested) via a scaled chi-square
# difference test. The two models are not nested in the strict lavaan sense
# (bifactor adds a factor rather than freeing parameters of mdl_3f), so treat
# the LRT as a secondary check and lean on the fit-index comparison + omega
# hierarchical below for the actual interpretation.
#
# NOTE: if bifactor-propriety-check above flagged fit_bifactor as improper,
# this comparison is not meaningful as a "which model is better" argument --
# an inadmissible model can show spuriously good fit indices.

fit_bifactor_tbl <- bind_rows(
  grab_fit(fit_3f, "Three correlated factors + age"),
  grab_fit(fit_bifactor, "Bifactor (g + 3 group factors) + age")
)

anova_bifactor <- tryCatch(
  anova(fit_3f, fit_bifactor),
  error = function(e) NULL
)
```

```{r bifactor-omega}
# Omega hierarchical / omega subscale: how much reliable variance in each
# group factor's indicators is attributable to g vs. the group factor itself.
# High omega-h for g (and low residual omega for the group factors) would
# support the "one general developmental factor" reading the reviewers raised;
# the opposite pattern would support the group factors as distinguishable
# constructs worth reporting separately.

# semTools::reliability() is deprecated in favor of compRelSEM(); also,
# omega on an improper (Heywood-case) solution isn't interpretable, so this
# is only worth reading if bifactor_proper (above) is TRUE.
omega_bifactor <- if (bifactor_proper) {
  tryCatch(semTools::compRelSEM(fit_bifactor, higher = "g"), error = function(e) {
    message("omega calculation failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })
} else {
  message("skipping omega: fit_bifactor is an improper solution")
  NULL
}
```

```{r bifactor-loadings-plot}
# Standardized loadings on g vs. on each group factor, for a quick visual
# gut-check of which indicators are mostly "general" vs. mostly "specific."
# Reuses the same plotting approach as the other SEM figures (parameterEstimates
# + tidySEM), so a proper node/edge layout (sem/layouts/bifactor_sem_layout.xlsx)
# will need to be created before this chunk can render a figure end-to-end.

pe_bifactor <- parameterEstimates(fit_bifactor, standardized = TRUE)

loadings_bifactor <- pe_bifactor |>
  filter(op == "=~") |>
  select(factor = lhs, indicator = rhs, std.all)
```
